answers.answer: Shuffle the Factory deck, select players + 1 cards face-down onto the board, and return the others to the box without looking. Put one randomly selected structure bonus tile face-up below the Popularity Track and place encounter tokens on each of the 11 marked territories. The lowest-numbered Player Mat starts; then play proceeds clockwise.
answers.evidence: Setup: 'randomly select number of players + 1' Factory cards; 'one encounter token on each of the 11 marked territories'; 'Randomly choose one structure bonus tile'; 'The lowest-numbered Player Mat starts.'

answers.answer: The Faction Mat sets starting power and starting combat-card draw; put the character on the home base, one worker on each of its two land-adjoined territories, four mechs over their abilities, and six stars by the emblem. The Player Mat sets starting popularity and starting coins and supplies two objective cards; also place six technology cubes, four structures, four recruits, and six remaining workers as directed by the mat. Starting power/cards come from the Faction Mat; popularity, coins, and objectives come from the Player Mat.
answers.evidence: Setup: 'Faction Mat: set starting power and draw starting combat cards'; 'Player Mat: set starting popularity and take starting coins and objectives ... (two objective cards).'

answers.answer: Yes, you may take neither action after moving the token to a different section; that is a dead turn if unable to afford any action. Only Rusviet may repeat a section. Top-row gains may pay the bottom-row cost. Bottom cannot be first if taking both: resolve top before bottom. Pay the full exposed red-box cost before taking any desired amount of green-box benefit; costs and benefits vary by Player Mat and upgrades. You must move the token to a different section from last turn.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: 'optionally take that section's top action once, then optionally its bottom action once'; 'bottom first is not allowed'; 'First pay the full cost'; 'You may use top-row gains to pay the bottom-row cost'; 'Rusviet may repeat a section.'

answers.answer: An enemy worker alone on your structure's territory controls the territory and its resources. Enemy units do not gain your structure's abilities; you retain those abilities even without control, except a Mill cannot produce on an uncontrolled territory. Pay action resources from any territories you currently control, even when acting elsewhere.
answers.evidence: Control section: 'An enemy worker alone on your structure's territory controls it and all its resources'; 'Enemy units do not gain your structure's abilities'; 'Pay costs using resources from any territories you currently control.'

answers.answer: No. A normal Move selects up to two different units, each moving one adjacent territory, and the same unit cannot use both selections to move twice. A transported worker can subsequently move itself, or move onto a mech and be carried by its later move. All units (characters, mechs, workers) can carry any number of resources; only mechs can also carry any number of your workers, never your character.
answers.evidence: Move: 'up to two different units, one adjacent territory each'; 'cannot use both selections to move the same unit twice'; carried worker 'may subsequently move itself'; 'Only mechs may also carry any number of your workers.'

answers.answer: A character or mech entering territory occupied only by enemy workers stops and cannot move again that turn; those workers immediately retreat to their home base, leaving resources. You lose one popularity per worker, down to zero; having zero or insufficient popularity does not stop the retreat. This is not combat. The mech's carried workers do not independently enter: a worker cannot independently enter enemy-worker-controlled territory.
answers.evidence: Move: character/mech entering 'enemy workers only' stops; workers 'immediately retreat'; 'Lose one popularity per worker, down to zero'; 'A worker cannot independently enter enemy-worker-controlled territory.'

answers.answer: After all units finish a Move action, resolve combats before the bottom-row action; the attacker chooses the order of multiple combats. A worker cannot independently move into or out of a territory controlled by enemy characters or mechs.
answers.evidence: Move: finish moving the other units, then resolve 'all combats before the bottom-row action; attacker chooses multiple-combat order'; workers cannot independently move 'into or out of' territory controlled by enemy characters/mechs.

answers.answer: Bolster costs $1 and gives two power or one combat card before upgrades. If the combat deck is empty, shuffle discards into a new deck; if both deck and discard are empty, draw none. Trade costs $1 and gives any two resources (same or different) or one popularity before upgrades. Put traded resources on a controlled territory containing at least one worker; if all workers are at home, you cannot Trade for resources. Built Monument adds one popularity to Bolster; built Armory adds one power to Trade.
answers.evidence: Bolster: 'Pay $1, gain two power OR one combat card'; exhausted deck: 'shuffle discards into a new deck'; Trade: 'Pay $1, gain any two resources ... OR one popularity'; resources go on a controlled territory 'containing at least one worker.'

answers.answer: Pay every exposed Produce cost (power, popularity and/or coins) in full before producing; you must afford all of it. Choose up to two different controlled territories, and each worker there may produce one token on its own territory; a controlled Mill is an additional bonus territory and produces as one worker. New workers come from the Player Mat left to right and are placed in the producing village. You may decline some or all production, including new workers. Workers exposed by producing change future Produce costs, not the cost already paid.
answers.evidence: Produce: 'Pay every exposed Produce cost ... before producing'; choose 'up to two different controlled territories'; new workers 'from the Player Mat left to right'; exposed costs affect 'future Produce actions, not the cost already paid'; may decline production.

answers.answer: Upgrade costs oil: move any technology cube from a green box to an empty bracketed red box, improving a top benefit and reducing a bottom cost; solid-black-bordered red boxes cannot be upgraded. Deploy costs metal: choose a mech and put it on a controlled territory with your worker, never a lake. Its uncovered ability then applies to your character and every mech, not workers. Even after completing all upgrades, mechs, structures, and recruits, you may still pay the bottom action to gain its coins and applicable ongoing recruit bonuses.
answers.evidence: Bottom-row actions: 'Upgrade — oil'; 'Deploy — metal'; mech goes to 'a controlled territory with your worker, never a lake'; 'may still pay for that bottom action to gain coins and applicable ongoing recruit bonuses.'

answers.answer: Build costs wood and puts a structure on a controlled territory with your worker; only one structure total may occupy a territory, including opponents' structures. Factory is allowed; lakes and home bases are forbidden. Structures cannot move or be destroyed. A Mill provides an additional Produce territory and produces as one worker only while you control its territory; it cannot produce when uncontrolled, including when an enemy occupies it. Your Mine is a personal tunnel for all your unit movement even when an enemy controls its territory; opponents cannot use your building abilities.
answers.evidence: Build: 'controlled territory with your worker'; 'Structures cannot be moved or destroyed'; Mill works 'only while controlled'; Mine is a personal tunnel 'even when enemy-controlled.'

answers.answer: Take a recruit from any bottom-row section of the Player Mat and put it permanently on any open one-time bonus space on the Faction Mat; immediately gain two power, two coins, two popularity, or two combat cards. The ongoing bonus is set by the circle uncovered where the recruit was removed, independent of the chosen one-time bonus: Upgrade gives one power, Deploy one coin, Build one popularity, Enlist one combat card. For a triggering bottom-row action by you or an immediate neighbor, resolve active player first, then left, then right; stop if a sixth star ends the game. In a two-player game the opponent triggers the bonus once, not twice.
answers.evidence: Enlist: recruit from 'any bottom-row section'; one-time bonus is 'two power, two coins, two popularity, or two combat cards'; ongoing bonus is the circle uncovered; resolve 'active player first, then left, then right'; two-player opponent triggers 'once, not twice.'

answers.answer: Each combatant secretly chooses dial power from zero to the smaller of seven and their current power, then may add up to one combat card per participating character/mech, even with zero dial power; Rusviet People's Army adds one additional card total if any workers are present. If both have combat mech abilities, attacker uses theirs first, then defender. Reveal simultaneously and total dial power plus card values; attacker wins ties. Each player deducts their dial power from their power track, and every played card is discarded face-up, regardless of who wins. Card values do not deduct additional track power.
answers.evidence: Combat: dial from '0 to the smaller of seven and your current power'; cards 'one ... per participating character/mech'; totals revealed simultaneously; 'attacker wins ties'; payment applies to winner and loser alike.

answers.answer: The winner controls the territory and resources and places an eligible combat star (ordinary maximum two; Saxony unrestricted within six available). All losing characters, mechs, and workers retreat to their own home base, leaving all resources on the battle territory; Nordic Seaworthy allows eligible units and carried workers to retreat to adjacent lakes instead. A winning attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat, including workers carried by a defeated mech on a lake; a winning defender loses none. Polania Camaraderie waives the loss only after winning combat as aggressor on their turn. The loser draws one combat card if they revealed at least one power on the dial or through cards; a zero-total loser draws none.
answers.evidence: Combat: losing units 'retreat to their own home base, leaving all resources'; winning attacker loses 'one popularity per enemy worker'; loser draws one card if they revealed power 'on the dial OR through cards.'

answers.answer: After the whole Move action and all combats, resolve the encounter if the character remains in the territory; discard the token and draw a card. If contested entry is lost, the character retreats and the token stays. Gains of resources, workers, mechs, or structures go to the encounter territory. Pay the selected option's printed cost, but no additional normal action costs or mat benefits apply, including no ongoing recruit bonuses.
answers.evidence: Encounters: after 'the whole Move action and all combats'; if character loses, 'the token stays'; gains go to 'the encounter territory'; 'Pay no additional normal action costs' or ongoing recruit bonuses.

answers.answer: Every player's character, on its first finish of a Move action at the Factory (after winning combat if needed), looks at available Factory cards, chooses one, and returns the rest. Each player may have at most one permanent card; later visits cannot exchange it. Use it as a fifth action section with optional top then bottom, following the normal no-repeat rule except for Rusviet. Factory actions grant no corresponding Player Mat coins, structure bonuses, or ongoing recruit bonuses. Factory bottom action moves one unit up to two territories within that Move action, or three for a Speed character/mech; Mine access and normal movement and stop restrictions apply.
answers.evidence: Factory: 'Every player's character' on its first finish of a Move action chooses one; 'later visits cannot exchange it'; bottom action moves 'one unit up to two territories ... or three ... with Speed.'

answers.answer: Only on your own turn, before or after completing a top or bottom action, may you reveal a completed objective; all requirements must be met at the moment of reveal. Place the objective star and put both objective cards on the bottom of the deck. Normally only one objective star is allowed; Saxony keeps the second card after the first objective and can score both.
answers.evidence: Objectives: 'Only on your own turn, before or after completing a top or bottom action'; meet 'all requirements at the moment of reveal'; place star and put 'both objective cards on the bottom'; Saxony retains the other card.

answers.answer: Stars are earned for six upgrades, four deployed mechs, four built structures, four recruits, all eight workers on the board, one revealed completed objective, combat victory (up to two stars except Saxony's unrestricted limit within six available), 18 popularity, or 16 power. Goals are awarded once except the two combat stars and Saxony exception. Stars are permanent even if power or popularity later drops, and another player's star does not block your goal. The sixth star immediately ends play, with no equalizing turns or further actions.
answers.evidence: Stars section lists the achievements; 'A placed star is permanent'; 'Other players' stars never block a goal'; 'sixth star immediately ends play.'

answers.answer: If a bottom-row action earns the sixth star, first collect the primary benefit, coins, and your ongoing recruit benefit, then place the star. If units remain intermingled in an unresolved battle, undo that part of movement and return initiating units to where they came from; do not resolve another combat. A neighbor's power/popularity recruit star can occur only after the active player finishes the action and only if no earlier sixth star ended the game; resolve in active, left, right order.
answers.evidence: Sixth star: collect 'primary benefit, coins and your ongoing recruit benefit before placing that star'; unresolved battle movement is undone; neighbors' recruit stars occur after active player and only if no earlier sixth star ended the game.

answers.answer: At 10 popularity, each star is $4, each controlled territory is $3, and each complete pair of controlled resources is $2. Five stars = $20; four ordinary territories plus Factory count as seven territories = $21; 13 resources yield six pairs = $12, for $53 added to held coins and any selected structure bonus. The selected structure bonus is earned even if enemies control your structure territories. Highest total coins wins. Tiebreakers, in order: workers + mechs + structures (not character), power, popularity, resources controlled, territories controlled, then stars placed.
answers.evidence: Final fortune table at popularity 7–12 gives $4/star, $3/territory, $2/per two resources; Factory counts as three territories. 'Structure bonus: Earn it even if enemies control' the territories; tiebreak list begins 'workers + mechs + structures' and ends with stars placed.
